title: Reversal Sets and Uniform Coverage for SACE Sensitivity Analysis in the Survival Odds Ratio
banked_reason: D0.5.G normalized the delivered inverse-reversal result to incremental, below the field floor: paper score ceiling 5.8 < 7.4; critical Gaussian optimality and finite-n transfer remain unproved.
gap_reasons: It does not prove optimality, a converse for confidence-set size, or any matched expected-width result, and the critical theta≈c/n Gaussian experiment is only defined rather than analyzed.
The binary-X, balanced-allocation, common-index restriction further makes the algebraic contribution too narrow for the field tier absent the deferred critical-regime optimality result.
proof_attempt_summary: The D-stage derivation proved an exact quadratic classification of natural SACE reversals in the binary-covariate, common-odds-ratio model, plus uniform outer coverage of the complete reversal set and conditional simple-root and double-root localization. The original adaptive simultaneous-band program was replaced at the accepted D-1 proposal gate by this inverse-set program. The delivered inference remains a conservative projection; an all-honest Gaussian lower bound, attaining rule, and finite-sample transfer at theta of order 1/n are still open, so the field novelty floor was not met.
tldr: For each declared survival odds ratio, the published identification formula yields the natural trial-prevalence SACE over the observed covariate distribution. In the strict binary-\(X\), balanced-allocation, common-scalar-index specialization, the inverse zero geometry is exactly quadratic in the positive cell-1 principal score: a feasibility filter and rational index map enumerate at most two isolated reversals, while explicit coefficient identities characterize the only identity case. A nine-coordinate primitive rectangle jointly estimates the covariate prevalence, four survival margins, and four survivor means; its projection gives uniform outer coverage of the complete natural reversal set and a first-reversal confidence set that retains the discrete no-crossing state. Simple crossings localize at \(n^{-1/2}\), double tangencies at \(n^{-1/4}\), and equal-cell standardization is only a diagnostic corollary.
gap: Published odds-ratio principal-stratification work identifies and estimates effects at a declared regular index, while general criterion-set and moment-inequality methods provide inversion and uniform-inference frameworks. None of these results derives the finite positive-principal-root elimination, branch filter, measurable component enumeration, and no-crossing state for the inverse equal-cell standardized SACE curve.
fill: The project supplies the feasible resultant with complete filtering, finite root isolation, uniform outer coverage of the full reversal set and first-reversal state, and a directional polynomial localization map driven by an explicit eight-coordinate influence vector.
